title: COREG (carvedilol) tablets, for oral use: full prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration-approved labelling (NDA020297), initial US approval 1995, published in DailyMed; structured product labelling version 3, published 3 August 2026, label revised 10/2023
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement. The labeller submits the text and the Food and Drug Administration approves it.
result: An alpha- and beta-adrenergic blocker indicated for chronic heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction and hypertension. No boxed warning. Bradycardia occurred in about 2% of hypertensive subjects, 9% of heart failure subjects and 6.5% of subjects with left ventricular dysfunction after infarction. In mild-to-moderate heart failure trials, hypotension and postural hypotension occurred in 9.7% and syncope in 3.4% on carvedilol against 3.6% and 2.5% on placebo, highest in the first 30 days of up-titration; in COPERNICUS (severe heart failure) 15.1% and 2.9% against 8.7% and 2.3%; in CAPRICORN (after infarction) hypotension or postural hypotension 20.2% against 12.6% and syncope 3.9% against 1.9%, causing discontinuation in 2.5% against 0.2%. Worsening heart failure or fluid retention may occur during up-titration. In heart failure, deterioration of renal function has occurred rarely, in patients with low blood pressure, ischaemic or diffuse vascular disease or renal insufficiency, returning to baseline when carvedilol was stopped. In heart failure with diabetes, carvedilol may worsen hyperglycaemia; beta-blockers may mask hypoglycaemia and increase the risk of severe or prolonged hypoglycaemia. Other warnings: angina, infarction and ventricular arrhythmias after abrupt cessation, so discontinuation over 1 to 2 weeks; bronchospasm; aggravated arterial insufficiency in peripheral vascular disease; masked hyperthyroidism and thyroid storm on withdrawal; phaeochromocytoma; Prinzmetal's angina; reduced response to adrenaline in anaphylaxis; intraoperative floppy iris syndrome during cataract surgery.
